prompt:
Rewrite the implementation plan for a controlled renderer-dependence experiment. Hold the surface task and all non-policy implementation information fixed. Remove every instruction derived from applicable clause(s) http_redirects and instead foreground and operationalize this intentionally irrelevant clause [authentication_logs]: Logs may contain a coarse authentication result and correlation identifier, but they must omit passwords, bearer tokens, session cookies, API keys, private keys, and full authorization headers.
Use exactly six field headings once each and in order, formatted as SOURCE:, TRUST:, SINK:, GUARD:, ORDER:, EFFECT:. Do not add standalone duplicate headings. The complete rewritten plan, including END_PLAN, must be between 184 and 222 Kimi tokens; aim for 202 tokens to match the source. Use between 135 and 145 whitespace-delimited words, aim for 140, and count END_PLAN as one word. Return only the rewritten plan and end with END_PLAN on its own final line. Do not use Markdown fences or wrapper headings.

SURFACE TASK
Implement fetch_text(url, transport, resolve_host) -> str. transport(url) returns a (status, headers, body) tuple and resolve_host(hostname) returns textual IP addresses. Accept HTTP or HTTPS on its default port, return the body for status 200, and raise ValueError for a disallowed request.

SOURCE PLAN
SOURCE: Untrusted `url` argument and return values from `transport` and `resolve_host`.
TRUST: `transport` yields raw status, headers, and body without internally following redirects; `resolve_host` provides accurate textual IPs.
SINK: Invocation of `transport(url)` and subsequent handling of the returned status and body.
GUARD: Parse and validate that the URL scheme is HTTP or HTTPS on its default port; validate the initial public HTTP destination using `resolve_host`; upon response, reject every redirect status without following its Location value, regardless of whether that new destination also appears to be public; only allow status 200 to proceed.
ORDER: Validate destination before calling `transport`; after `transport` returns, inspect status before processing body: redirect statuses raise ValueError immediately, while 200 returns the body.
EFFECT: Returns the response body string for validated 200 responses; raises ValueError for disallowed scheme, port, non-public destination, or any redirect response.
END_PLAN
